zh.title: 雅可比矩阵
summary: 1、学习了雅克比(Jacobean)矩阵的推导，雅克比矩阵用于在已知各个关节角速度的情况下，计算末端执行器的速度(3维角速度+3维线速度)。雅克比矩阵的行数等于末端执行器的自由度，列数等于关节的自由度。

2、雅克比矩阵的推导方法有两种：
     ✅ 通过关节空间速度的线性组合来推导雅克比矩阵。
     ✅ 通过末端执行器的位姿对关节空间的偏导数来推导雅克比矩阵。

3、雅克比矩阵的物理意义：
     ✅ 雅克比矩阵的每一列对应一个关节的速度对末端执行器速度的贡献，即仅第 i 关节以单位速度转动，其余全部锁死，得到的末端 6 维 twist。
     ✅ 雅克比矩阵的每一行对应末端执行器在某个方向上的速度对关节速度的敏感性。

4、雅克比矩阵的奇异性：
     ✅ 当雅克比矩阵的行列式为零时，机器人处于奇异位置，此时末端执行器的某些方向上的速度无法通过关节速度来实现。
     ✅ 奇异位置可能导致控制问题和运动规划困难。

5、雅克比矩阵的两种形式：
     ✅ 空间雅克比矩阵（Space Jacobian）J_{s}：描述末端执行器在空间坐标系下的速度与关节速度之间的关系。
     ✅ 物体雅克比矩阵（Body Jacobian）J_{b}：描述末端执行器在自身坐标系下的速度与关节速度之间的关系。
     ✅ 参考坐标系变换（change of reference frame）：𝒱_{s} = Ad(T_{sb})𝒱_{b}，其中 T_{sb} 是末端坐标系相对于基座坐标系的齐次变换矩阵。

6、机器人静力学：
     核心公式：τ = J_{b}^{T}(θ)ℱ_{b}
     ✅ τ：n 维关节力矩向量，表示各关节电机需要输出的力矩。
     ✅ ℱ_{b}：在末端工具坐标系 {b} 下描述的 6 维力旋量（wrench），[m; f] = [m_{x}, m_{y}, m_{z}, f_{x}, f_{y}, f_{z}]^{T}，由 3 个力矩分量和 3 个力分量组成。
     ✅ J_{b}^{T}：物体雅可比矩阵（Body Jacobian）J_{b} 的转置。
     ✅ 雅可比J用来向前映射速度；雅可比的转置J^{T}用来向后映射力/力矩。
     ✅  运动学：给电机转速，算出手怎么动；J做正向映射。  静力学：我想要手推多大的力，反推每个电机需要输出多大扭矩；用J^{T}。

7、奇异位形：
     ✅ 某个关节角度θ下，雅克比矩阵J降秩，机器人处于奇异位形。
     ✅ 奇异是瞬时自由度丢失，不是完全到不了这个空间点；你可以绕路到达该空间点，只是在这个特定姿态下，瞬时不能朝某方向运动。
     ✅ J_{s}与J_{b}如果有一个奇异，则另一个一定奇异；伴随变换Ad_{T}可逆，不改变矩阵秩。
     ✅ 运动学层面：丢失一个或多个方向的瞬时运动能力，有些方向末端无论电机怎么动，都产生不了该方向速度。
     ✅ 静力学层面：某些末端力旋量方向，无论关节输出多大的关节力矩，都无法在末端产生这个方向的力。

8、可操作度：
     ✅ 可操作度是奇异位形的量化指标，用于描述机器人当前位姿距离奇异状态有多远，通常使用椭球进行可视化。
     ✅ 可操作度越小，说明机器人在当前姿态下的运动能力越差，也越接近奇异位形。
     ✅ 两个核心椭球：速度可操作椭球和力椭球。
     ✅ 速度可操作椭球：约束条件是关节角速度存在上限，即电机转速不能无限增大。
        • 长轴方向：只需给关节较为普通的转速，末端执行器便能产生较大的速度，说明该方向的运动能力较强。
        • 短轴方向：即使关节以很高的速度运动，末端执行器在该方向上也难以产生明显速度，说明该方向接近奇异。
        • 当机器人到达奇异位形时，椭球会沿某个方向被压缩；若某根半轴长度为 0，则末端执行器完全无法沿该方向瞬时运动。
     ✅ 力椭球：约束条件是关节输出力矩存在上限，即电机能够提供的力矩有限。
        • 长轴方向：只需施加较为普通的关节力矩，末端执行器便能产生较大的力，说明该方向的力输出能力较强。
        • 短轴方向：即使关节输出很大的力矩，末端执行器在该方向上也难以产生明显的力。
     ✅ 速度可操作椭球与力椭球具有相同的主轴方向，但对应半轴长度互为倒数：速度椭球越长的方向，力椭球越短；速度椭球越短的方向，力椭球越长。

en.title: Jacobian Matrix
summary: 1. I studied the derivation of the Jacobian matrix. Given the angular velocities of all joints, the Jacobian maps joint velocities to the velocity of the end effector. Its number of rows equals the degrees of freedom of the end effector, while its number of columns equals the number of joint degrees of freedom.

2. There are two common ways to derive the Jacobian matrix:
     ✅ Express the end-effector velocity as a linear combination of the joint-space velocities.
     ✅ Differentiate the end-effector pose with respect to the joint variables.

3. Physical interpretation of the Jacobian matrix:
     ✅ Each column describes how one joint contributes to the end-effector velocity: all other joints are locked while joint i moves at unit velocity, producing the corresponding six-dimensional end-effector twist.
     ✅ Each row describes how sensitive one component of the end-effector velocity is to the joint velocities.

4. Jacobian singularities:
     ✅ When the Jacobian loses rank (and, for a square Jacobian, its determinant is zero), the robot is in a singular configuration. Some directions of end-effector motion can no longer be generated through joint velocities.
     ✅ Singular configurations can create control problems and make motion planning more difficult.

5. Two forms of the Jacobian matrix:
     ✅ The space Jacobian J_{s} relates joint velocities to the end-effector velocity expressed in the space frame.
     ✅ The body Jacobian J_{b} relates joint velocities to the end-effector velocity expressed in the body frame.
     ✅ Change of reference frame: 𝒱_{s} = Ad(T_{sb})𝒱_{b}, where T_{sb} is the homogeneous transformation of the end-effector frame relative to the base frame.

6. Robot statics:
     Core equation: τ = J_{b}^{T}(θ)ℱ_{b}
     ✅ τ: an n-dimensional vector of joint torques, representing the torque that each joint actuator must produce.
     ✅ ℱ_{b}: a six-dimensional wrench expressed in the end-effector frame {b}, [m; f] = [m_{x}, m_{y}, m_{z}, f_{x}, f_{y}, f_{z}]^{T}, consisting of three moment components and three force components.
     ✅ J_{b}^{T}: the transpose of the body Jacobian J_{b}.
     ✅ The Jacobian J maps velocities forward, whereas its transpose J^{T} maps forces and torques backward.
     ✅ Kinematics: given the joint velocities, use J to determine how the end effector moves. Statics: given a desired end-effector wrench, use J^{T} to determine the torque required from each joint actuator.

7. Singular configurations:
     ✅ At a particular joint configuration θ, the robot is in a singular configuration when the Jacobian J loses rank.
     ✅ A singularity represents an instantaneous loss of one or more degrees of freedom; it does not mean that the corresponding point in space is completely unreachable. The robot may reach that point along another path, but at the singular configuration it cannot instantaneously move in certain directions.
     ✅ If either J_{s} or J_{b} is singular, the other must also be singular because the adjoint transformation Ad_{T} is invertible and therefore preserves matrix rank.
     ✅ From a kinematic perspective, the robot loses instantaneous mobility in one or more directions: no combination of joint velocities can produce end-effector velocity in those directions.
     ✅ From a static perspective, certain end-effector wrench directions cannot be produced, regardless of the joint torques applied.

8. Manipulability:
     ✅ Manipulability quantifies how close the current robot configuration is to a singularity and is commonly visualized using ellipsoids.
     ✅ A smaller manipulability value indicates poorer motion capability at the current configuration and greater proximity to a singularity.
     ✅ Two key ellipsoids are used: the velocity manipulability ellipsoid and the force ellipsoid.
     ✅ Velocity manipulability ellipsoid: joint velocities are bounded because the actuators cannot rotate arbitrarily fast.
        • Long-axis direction: moderate joint velocities can generate a high end-effector velocity, indicating strong motion capability in that direction.
        • Short-axis direction: even very high joint velocities produce little end-effector velocity, indicating that the direction is close to singular.
        • At a singular configuration, the ellipsoid collapses along at least one direction. If a semi-axis has zero length, the end effector cannot move instantaneously in that direction.
     ✅ Force ellipsoid: joint torques are bounded because each actuator has a finite torque capacity.
        • Long-axis direction: moderate joint torques can generate a large end-effector force, indicating strong force capability in that direction.
        • Short-axis direction: even large joint torques produce little end-effector force in that direction.
     ✅ The velocity and force ellipsoids have the same principal-axis directions, but their corresponding semi-axis lengths are reciprocals: a direction in which the velocity ellipsoid is long is short in the force ellipsoid, and vice versa.
